title: Multiplying and dividing fractions and mixed numbers
blurb: Multiply and divide fractions and mixed numbers by hand: convert to improper fractions first, cross-cancel, and multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor.
question: A hospital kitchen has 5 1/3 cups of oats, and each batch of oatmeal uses 2/3 cup. How many batches can be made, and which operation gets you there?

teach.body: Formally, a/b × c/d = (a × c)/(b × d), and a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c, where d/c is the reciprocal of the divisor. In plain English: to multiply, multiply straight across; to divide, flip the second fraction and multiply. Unlike adding, neither needs a common denominator, but both need mixed numbers turned into improper fractions first. The HESI A2 calculator has no fraction key, so you do these by hand.

items: Cross-cancel: the 5 on top and the 5 on the bottom cancel, leaving 1/2 × 8/1.

teach.caption: Canceling first keeps the numbers small: 12/72 also simplifies to 1/6, but takes longer.

teach.body: The reciprocal of a fraction swaps its numerator and denominator: 3/8 → 8/3. A number times its reciprocal is 1. A whole number n is n/1, so its reciprocal is 1/n (the reciprocal of 4 is 1/4). A mixed number must become an improper fraction before it is flipped: 2 2/5 = 12/5, so its reciprocal is 5/12, not 5/2 or 5/22.

teach.caption: Only the second fraction (the divisor) flips. Check: 2/3 × 9/8 = 18/24 = 3/4. ✓

teach.h: Which operation does the story need?

teach.text: Three classic slips: multiplying mixed numbers part by part (2 1/2 × 4 is 10, not 8 1/2); flipping the wrong fraction, or both, when dividing; and multiplying when the story asks how many pieces fit, which gives a smaller answer when a larger one makes sense.

teach.body: Priya Patel, a nursing applicant working in a hospital kitchen, has 5 1/3 cups of oats and each batch needs 2/3 cup. "How many 2/3s fit in 5 1/3?" means divide. 5 1/3 = 16/3. Keep, change, flip: 16/3 × 3/2 = 48/6 = 8. Check: 8 × 2/3 = 16/3 = 5 1/3. ✓ She can make 8 batches.

items: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions before multiplying or dividing.
Multiply: cross-cancel, then top × top and bottom × bottom.
Divide: keep the first, change ÷ to ×, flip the second.
"Of" means multiply; "how many fit" means divide.
Simplify the answer and check it with the inverse operation.

summary: You can now multiply and divide fractions and mixed numbers by hand: convert to improper fractions, cross-cancel, and multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor. You can tell from the story which operation is needed and avoid the part-by-part and wrong-flip slips the HESI A2 turns into wrong answers.

A.q: A recipe uses 3/4 cup of milk per batch. How much milk is needed for 2 1/2 batches?
A.why: Convert: 2 1/2 = 5/2. Then 3/4 × 5/2 = 15/8 = 1 7/8 cups. Check: 2 batches use 1 1/2 cups and half a batch uses 3/8 cup; 1 4/8 + 3/8 = 1 7/8.

whyNot.0: 2 3/8 multiplies only the 1/2 by 3/4 (3/8) and keeps the 2, instead of converting 2 1/2 first.
whyNot.1: 3 1/4 adds 3/4 and 2 1/2; "per batch" for several batches calls for multiplying.
whyNot.2: 1 1/2 is the milk for 2 batches only; the half batch is missing.

A.q: A bottle holds 12 tablespoons of liquid antacid. Each dose is 3/4 tablespoon. How many doses are in the bottle?

whyNot.0: 9 is 12 × 3/4: it multiplies by the dose instead of dividing by it.
whyNot.2: 36 multiplies by the numerator 3 instead of by the flipped fraction 4/3.
whyNot.3: 48 multiplies by 4 but forgets to divide by 3.

whyNot.0: 13/4 is 3 1/4 as an improper fraction; it has not been flipped.
whyNot.1: 4 flips only the fraction part 1/4 and drops the whole number 3.
whyNot.3: 4/31 reads 3 1/4 as 31/4 before flipping; the improper fraction is 13/4.

whyNot.0: 4 1/3 multiplies only the fraction part (2/3 × 1/2 = 1/3) and keeps the whole 4.
whyNot.3: 6 3/4 flips the first fraction before multiplying (3/2 × 9/2 = 27/4).

B.q: A 7 1/2-foot length of tubing is cut into pieces that are each 3/4 foot long. How many pieces are cut?

whyNot.1: 9 1/3 divides only the whole number 7 by 3/4 and drops the 1/2 foot.
whyNot.3: 1/10 flips the first fraction instead of the divisor (2/15 × 3/4).

B.q: Which expression has the same value as 4/9 ÷ 2/3?
B.why: Keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, flip the divisor: 4/9 × 3/2 = 12/18 = 2/3.

whyNot.1: This flips the first fraction (the dividend) instead of the divisor.
whyNot.2: This flips both fractions; only the divisor flips.
whyNot.3: This changes ÷ to × without flipping anything, which multiplies instead of divides.

C.q: Each batch of bran muffins uses 2 1/4 cups of flour. How much flour is needed for 2 2/3 batches?
C.why: Convert: 2 1/4 = 9/4 and 2 2/3 = 8/3. Multiply: 9/4 × 8/3 = 72/12 = 6 cups. Cross-cancel check: (3/1) × (2/1) = 6.

whyNot.1: 4 1/6 multiplies the wholes (2 × 2) and the fractions (1/4 × 2/3) separately; mixed numbers must be converted first.
whyNot.2: 4 11/12 adds the two mixed numbers instead of multiplying.
whyNot.3: 27/32 divides 9/4 by 8/3; "per batch" for several batches calls for multiplying.

C.q: A 2 1/4-cup container of formula is divided equally among 6 bottles. A baby drinks 2/3 of one bottle. How many cups does the baby drink?
C.why: Each bottle: 9/4 ÷ 6 = 9/4 × 1/6 = 9/24 = 3/8 cup. The baby drinks 2/3 × 3/8 = 6/24 = 1/4 cup.

whyNot.0: 3/8 cup is one full bottle, one step short of the answer.
whyNot.2: 9/16 divides 3/8 by 2/3 instead of taking 2/3 of it.
whyNot.3: 1 1/2 takes 2/3 of the whole 2 1/4-cup container (2/3 × 9/4) and skips sharing it among the 6 bottles.

whyNot.0: 6 ÷ 1/2 = 6 × 2 = 12. Dividing by a fraction less than 1 gives a larger number; 3 is 6 × 1/2.
whyNot.3: 1/2 × 2 1/2 = 1/2 × 5/2 = 5/4 = 1 1/4; 1 1/2 comes from multiplying only the whole number.

reteach.title: Division is "how many fit?"
reteach.question: How many quarters are in $3, and why does dividing by a fraction give a bigger number than you started with?

blocks.body: "How many quarters in $3?" is 3 ÷ 1/4. Each dollar holds 4 quarters, so 3 dollars hold 3 × 4 = 12. That is keep, change, flip: 3 ÷ 1/4 = 3 × 4/1 = 12. Dividing by a piece smaller than 1 asks how many small pieces fit, so the answer grows. Multiplying by a fraction does the opposite: 1/4 of $3 is 75 cents, a part of what you had.

items: How many 3/4-cup scoops in 6 cups? 6 ÷ 3/4 = 6 × 4/3 = 8 scoops.
How much is 3/4 of a 6-cup pot? 6 × 3/4 = 4 1/2 cups.
Check the size: 8 scoops is more than 6; 4 1/2 cups is less than 6.

blocks.text: If a "how many fit" answer comes out smaller than the amount you started with, you multiplied instead of dividing.

explain.body: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions, cancel any top with any bottom that share a factor, then multiply straight across. No common denominator needed.

whyNot.0: 1 1/8 multiplies only the fraction part (1/3 × 3/8 = 1/8) and keeps the whole 1.
whyNot.1: 32/9 is 4/3 × 8/3: it flips the second fraction, which is division.
whyNot.3: 7/11 adds the numerators and denominators of 4/3 and 3/8.

explain.body: Convert first, then flip the whole improper fraction. 1 2/3 = 5/3, so its reciprocal is 3/5. Check: 5/3 × 3/5 = 1.

whyNot.0: 5/3 is 1 2/3 as an improper fraction; it has not been flipped.
whyNot.2: 3/2 flips only the fraction part 2/3 and drops the whole number.
whyNot.3: 3/12 reads 1 2/3 as 12/3 before flipping; the improper fraction is 5/3.

explain.body: Keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, flip the second (the divisor). Only the divisor flips. 5/6 ÷ 2/3 = 5/6 × 3/2.

whyNot.2: 4/5 flips the first fraction instead of the divisor: 6/5 × 2/3.

explain.body: Convert both mixed numbers, then keep, change, flip. Dividing the whole parts and the fraction parts separately does not work. 2 1/2 ÷ 1 1/4 = 5/2 × 4/5 = 2.

whyNot.0: 4 divides the parts separately (2 ÷ 1 = 2 and 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 2) and adds them.
whyNot.2: 1/2 flips the first fraction instead of the divisor (2/5 × 5/4).
